sections.h2: Where is East Haven and how is the town laid out?
sections.html:
East Haven is a shoreline town in New Haven County, about 3 miles east of New Haven, with Long Island Sound on its southern edge. It covers 13.4 square miles, of which 1.2 are water, and the 2020 Census counted 27,923 residents.

On a map the town is taller than it is wide. It borders New Haven on the west, North Haven on the north, and Branford, North Branford and Lake Saltonstall on the east. East Haven shares Tweed New Haven Airport and the Alling Memorial Golf Course with New Haven. It also includes Stony Island, offshore from the town beach.

East Haven is about 35 miles from Hartford and 82 miles from New York City. The Connecticut Colony granted township here in May 1707, replacing the earlier name of Iron Works Village, and the town was incorporated in 1785.

sections.h2: What are the sections of East Haven?
sections.html:
Residents split East Haven into three large sections instead of many small neighborhoods. Each has a different character, and that shows up in buyer questions.

  • Foxon: the hilliest part of town, in the north and east around State Route 80. It holds the high school and Foxon Park Beverage.
  • Momauguin: the southern shore section, with the town beach, condominiums, summer cottages and an industrial park near the airport.
  • The Center: the administrative hub, with Town Hall, the fire department headquarters, Hagaman Memorial Library and the Old Stone Church, built in 1774. It includes the West End, next to New Haven.

A shoreline cottage in Momauguin, a hillside house in Foxon and an older house in the West End will draw very different questions. Tell us the section when you contact us.

sections.h2: How do storms and the Sound affect East Haven houses?
sections.html:
East Haven's climate is tempered by Long Island Sound, so winters are milder and snow is lighter than inland, but storms are a real part of owning a shoreline house. The town averages about 27 inches of snow in a normal winter and about 45 inches of precipitation a year.

Sellers near the water should expect buyers and insurers to ask about flood exposure. Ask the town about the flood zone for your lot, and gather any elevation certificate or insurance history you have.

sections.h2: What roads and transit serve East Haven?
sections.html:
Interstate 95 crosses the central part of East Haven, and U.S. Route 1 runs through the Center alongside it. State Routes 80, 100 and 142 also cross the town, with Route 80 running east to west through Foxon.

East Haven has no train station of its own. Union Station in New Haven is about 3 miles from the center of town, with Amtrak service, and a commuter station in Branford is the same distance away. Connecticut Transit buses serve the town, and Tweed New Haven Regional Airport sits on the border with New Haven.

The town has no hospital. Yale New Haven Hospital and related facilities are 3 to 5 miles away in New Haven, and the town runs the East Haven Public School system and the Hagaman Memorial Library.

sections.h2: What utilities serve an East Haven house?
sections.html:
East Haven is served by regional utilities, so closing paperwork often involves several accounts. These are the providers named for the town:

  • Water: the Regional Water Authority, from Lake Saltonstall in the south and Lake Gaillard in the north
  • Sewage: the New Haven Regional Water Pollution Control Authority
  • Electric: United Illuminating
  • Natural gas: Southern Connecticut Gas, with local propane distributors in some sections

If your house uses propane, ask the supplier about a final reading and about who owns the tank before closing.

sections.h2: When are East Haven property taxes due, and what is the mill rate?
sections.html:
East Haven taxes real estate and personal property at 35.78 mills on the 2025 Grand List, and motor vehicles at 32.46 mills. The town mailed bills around June 18, 2026, with the first installment due July 1, 2026 and payable without penalty through August 3, 2026.

ItemEast Haven detail
Mill rate, real estate and personal property35.78
Mill rate, motor vehicles32.46
First installment dueJuly 1, 2026 (grace through August 3, 2026)
Second installmentJanuary 2027
Bill mailingone bill a year, even when billed in two installments
Card payment fee2.99% or $3.95, whichever is greater

Taxpayers with an annual total of $200 or more receive two coupons and may pay in one or two installments. The tax office is at 250 Main Street, Town Hall upper level, phone 203-468-3307. Missing a bill in the mail does not excuse a late payment.

sections.h2: How does East Haven assess property, and what is the revaluation?
sections.html:
The East Haven Assessor records and values every real, personal and motor vehicle property, then files the Grand List with the Town Clerk by January 31 and with the state by May 1. Connecticut requires town-wide revaluations every five years.

The assessor's page lists a 2026 revaluation among its documents, along with a brochure from the contracted valuation company. Because new values change the tax a buyer will pay, call the assessor at 203-468-3233 for the current status and the appeal steps. The office is on the upper level of Town Hall at 250 Main Street.

sections.h2: What state filing applies when you sell in East Haven?
sections.html:
The seller or the seller's attorney files Connecticut's real estate conveyance tax return at recording, and tax is due when the price is $2,000 or more unless an exemption applies. East Haven is town code 044 on the state's list.

  • A transfer between spouses is exempt.
  • A principal residence sold for less than the mortgages and priority taxes owed on it can be exempt.
  • A deed in lieu of foreclosure on a principal residence can be exempt.

Your closing attorney sets the exact amount and the codes. Ask early, because the return goes with the deed.

sections.h2: What do East Haven sellers face, and how does a cash sale work?
sections.html:
East Haven sellers may be dealing with a shore cottage that needs storm repairs, an older house, an inherited house, or a loan that has fallen behind. A cash sale takes the house as it stands.

  • You send the address and describe the condition.
  • We review the facts and make an offer for the house as is.
  • A title company or closing attorney prepares the deed and the state return.
  • Open taxes, utility balances and liens are settled from the proceeds.

We do not state a price before looking at the property. Compare any offer with a listing before you decide.

faqs.q: What county is East Haven in?
faqs.a: East Haven is in New Haven County, about 3 miles east of New Haven.

faqs.q: What is East Haven's mill rate?
faqs.a: The mill rate for the 2025 Grand List is 35.78 for real estate and personal property and 32.46 for motor vehicles.

faqs.q: When are East Haven taxes due?
faqs.a: The first installment of the 2025 Grand List bills was due July 1, 2026, payable without penalty through August 3, 2026. Bills of $200 or more can be split, with the second installment due in January 2027.

faqs.q: Is East Haven's flood risk a concern when selling?
faqs.a: It can be. The town sits on Long Island Sound and Hurricane Irene destroyed houses along Cosey Beach in 2011, so buyers often ask about flood zone and insurance.

faqs.q: Can I sell an East Haven house that has storm damage?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can buy a house as it stands, with damage and deferred repairs included.

faqs.q: Who do I contact about my East Haven assessment?
faqs.a: Call the East Haven Assessor at 203-468-3233 or visit 250 Main Street, upper level of Town Hall.
